evidence.title: Covington and Burling: second ITC determination against IRICO increases legal and supply-chain risks for downstream companies using IRICO LCD glass
evidence.excerpt: On 6 August 2026 the Commission affirmed the initial determination in the glass-composition patents case and issued a Limited Exclusion Order prohibiting importation of certain IRICO glass AND products containing such glass, together with a Cease and Desist Order against the remaining importer respondent. The remedy explicitly covers TVs, monitors and computers. Downstream risks named: import disruption, customs scrutiny, certification burdens, sourcing uncertainty.

evidence.title: DigiTimes: Corning scores key ITC win in display glass IP defence against IRICO
evidence.excerpt: Frames the case as IP and trade-secret enforcement rather than as a trade measure or tariff story. Names the 7 April ALJ determination on the composition patents with a recommended Limited Exclusion Order, the 24 July initial determination on trade secrets, and a 16 April Unified Patent Court ruling in Germany. Corning's Brendan Mosher is quoted on the trade-secrets determination; no downstream company is named, only LCD TV and monitor manufacturers generically.

evidence.title: DigiTimes: Corning-IRICO trade secret case enters new phase
evidence.excerpt: The parallel trade-secret investigation continues: the public version of the initial determination issued on 13 August 2026, with the ALJ recommending exclusion orders against all remaining respondents and a cease-and-desist order. Subject to Commission review those orders would take effect in January 2027. The framing throughout is patent and trade-secret enforcement over fusion-draw technology.

evidence.title: Kellogg Hansen (counsel to Corning): Corning wins trade secrets initial determination at the ITC
evidence.excerpt: Counsel's announcement of the 24 July trade-secrets initial determination, describing misappropriation of Corning's proprietary fusion-draw technology for LCD glass substrates used in TVs, monitors, notebooks and tablets. Recorded here because it is counsel speaking, not the company: it is not a statement by Corning in its own name about the 6 August determination.

evidence.title: USITC: institution of the second Section 337 investigation into glass substrates for liquid crystal displays and products containing the same
evidence.excerpt: The investigation's own title carries the scope question this round called wrong: 'Certain Glass Substrates for Liquid Crystal Displays, Products Containing the Same, and Methods for Manufacturing the Same'. Products containing the same were named in the caption from institution, eighteen months before the order.

evidence.title: Daily closes for GLW, 600707.SS, 5201.T, 5214.T, 000725.SZ and LPL around 6 August 2026 (read through the harness price carrier)
evidence.excerpt: Corning closed -0.06%, +5.02% and -5.13% on 6, 7 and 10 August against a 60-session empirical band of 10.6%: inside it on every session. IRICO closed +3.03%, +3.27%, -1.80% against a band of about 10%, also inside, and its two largest moves are smaller than Corning's. AGC, NEG, BOE and LG Display all stayed inside their own bands across the five sessions.

resolutions.scorer_note: Both limbs wrong, and the second one was checkable before the lock. The Limited Exclusion Order of 6 August prohibits importation of IRICO glass AND products containing such glass, explicitly reaching TVs, monitors and computers; a Cease and Desist Order issued against the remaining importer respondent. The investigation has been captioned 'Glass Substrates ... Products Containing the Same' since institution in March 2025, so the downstream reach was in the case name eighteen months before the order and the operator did not look at the caption. The baseline (an exclusion order on a component stops the finished goods that contain it) had it.

The narrative row is due first and is scored first. DigiTimes frames the episode as IP and trade-secret enforcement over fusion-draw technology throughout, names the April patent determination and the German UPC ruling alongside it, and quotes Corning on innovation rather than on China. No account in the window frames it as a trade or tariff measure. The baseline (any US measure naming a Chinese company is reported as trade policy) missed.

Not established either way. Corning's counsel announced the July trade-secrets determination and Corning's Brendan Mosher is quoted on that one, but no statement by Corning in its own name about the 6 August patents determination was found inside the five days. Counsel speaking is not the company speaking, and the base rate cited (18 of 20 that a listed party confirms a regulatory step within five days) is about the company. Corning's IR feed was not read directly, so this is thin coverage rather than an absence.

Corning closed -0.06%, +5.02% and -5.13% on 6, 7 and 10 August, inside a 60-session empirical band of 10.6% on every session, and no carrier attributes any of it to the order. The visibility ratio operated exactly as cited. The honest qualification, which the round records against itself: a band that wide makes this absence call very cheap. Corning had daily moves of -13.6% and +15.7% in the sixty sessions before the event, so an order worth a fraction of a per cent could not have shown up whatever happened. That is the surviving-risk finding restated as a score.

The ordering failed. IRICO closed +3.03%, +3.27% and -1.80% over the three sessions; Corning closed -0.06%, +5.02% and -5.13%. The complainant's moves are the larger on two of three days and on the cumulative range, and the respondent's largest move is smaller than the complainant's smallest large one. The mechanism is scored wrong: the visibility ratio was cited to argue that the same order is the whole of the respondent's exposure and a fraction of the complainant's, and the ratio that actually mattered was ambient variance, which is far higher on Corning. The baseline (the larger company moves more because more money follows it) had it. Note also the direction: the respondent rose after being barred.

No CBP ruling, message or guidance naming finished displays as within the order's scope was found inside forty-five days. Scored thin and with a caveat that matters more than the score: the order itself already reaches products containing the glass, so the absence of a separate customs instrument is a narrow technical pass on a call whose spirit the map call already lost. An absence read off search summaries rather than off CBP's own rulings database is worth less than the same absence read off the register. Scored early: the window runs past today, and the call is resolved on what the record shows at 8 September rather than left open, with the remaining days named as the reason it can still turn.

The exact effective date for the patents-case order was not established, so the band is scored on the shape rather than on a date, at thin coverage. AGC closed inside its 4.8% band on all five sessions from 6 August (+0.01, +0.08, +0.71, +0.10, +0.79%), and Nippon Electric Glass did the same inside 5.4%. Nothing attributes a move at either substitute supplier to the order. The substitute's gain is real and is far too small to see against a diversified group's own variance, which is what the call said.

BOE closed inside its 9.0% band across the five sessions (-1.17, +0.82, -3.94, -0.67, -0.67%) with nothing attributed. The re-qualification cost of one substrate supplier does not reach a panel maker's price, as called. Recorded against the round: BOE's band could not be qualified for liquidity because the FX table carried no CNY rate when the backfill ran, so its observations carry band_reliable = null rather than true.
